# Generating an item crosses three gates: codebook, model distribution, and legal catalog

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-04 · 64 topic entries / 9 representative comparisons

TIGER converts items to hierarchical codes and learns the next code sequence. COBRA adds a conditioned dense vector after sparse codes. PLUM continues pretraining an existing LLM in behavior and SID space. STATIC changes how legal decoding executes without changing representation; Reward Guided Decoding tilts existing support toward business preferences. Locate the changed gate before assuming an omitted item can be recovered. PinGER separates historical inputs from SID supervision and treats prefix diversity, hierarchical DPO, and catalog legality separately.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Check item reachability before ranking quality

TIGER and PLUM determine item-to-SID mappings and step probabilities. COBRA recovers detail within nominated sparse regions. Unresolved collisions, pruned prefixes, or catalog omissions cannot be fixed simply by increasing reward weight. Measure token prediction, valid item coverage, and final ranking separately. A wider beam is not proof of a better codebook.

Sources: [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en.md) · [Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations](../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en.md) · [Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en.md)

### Legality and preference are different scores

STATIC decides which tokens can continue a prefix to a valid item. Reward Guided Decoding tilts the allowed distribution toward a reward. Negative infinity defines the feasible set; exponential tilting is a soft preference. A finite stock-violation penalty can still admit a high-reward invalid item. Keep constraint compilation, model probability, and business value distinct.

Sources: [Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators](../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en.md) · [Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

PailitaoMMSearch2.0 directly decodes multi-intent image/text requests into item SID sets, scaling serving with data tools, continual pretraining, mixed-budget SFT, and intent-balanced RL. Sample–Beam aligns inference sampling and beam candidate generation with training and display needs respectively. Larger models or longer reasoning do not guarantee improvement on every intent. Compare on fixed candidate sets, budgets, and production blending rules rather than model names. The full system is not reproduced locally.

Sources: [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36958-pailitao-mmsearch2/README-en.md)

### History inputs, candidate coverage, and legal paths have separate costs

TIGER represents historical items as multilevel SIDs. PinGER keeps levelwise SID supervision but restricts the backbone so later items see only historical dense inputs. Those dense inputs can still fuse SID information. PinGER's LCP penalty spreads beam slots across prefixes; it does not exclude nonexistent SIDs. STATIC compiles legal transitions. Greater spread has a trade-off: at λ=3 the paper reports higher distinct@1 and lower R@100. Do not attribute full-stack online lift to local mask or DPO components.

Sources: [PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en.md) · [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators](../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en.md)

### Shared computation, output objects and candidate diversification are separate decisions

TIGER turns items into semantic-code paths. ReuseGR retains SID hierarchy but shares query-prefix planning across users while current history still affects suffixes. SPADE instead generates executable free-text queries: OA-BPE changes tokenization priors, then parent-rank bonuses affect search survival; this is not PinGER common-SID-prefix penalization. Fix candidate budgets and output objects before comparing history-input, offline-planning and online-decoding costs. Reachable prefix coverage is not complete retrieval improvement.

Sources: [ReuseGR: Offline–Online Decoupled Generative Retrieval via Adaptive Prefix Reuse](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04259-reusegr/README-en.md) · [SPADE: Spatiotemporal Preference Alignment and Diversity Enhancement for Local Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04662-spade-local-search/README-en.md) · [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why can't COBRA's dense vector guarantee recovery of items missed early in a TIGER-style code path? {#cross-dense-cannot-recover-pruned-code}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** COBRA conditions dense queries on sparse codes, usually reranking within regions the beam nominated. If a target code is absent, the dense stage does not automatically search all omitted regions. It restores fine-grained distinction within a quantized region rather than repairing arbitrary recall misses.

    **Illustrative example:** If the first beam keeps only running shoes and prunes photography, perfect dense ranking of shoes will not retrieve a camera.

    Sources: [Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations](../../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en.md) · [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md)

### How should we interpret a conflict between STATIC's legal mask and high reward in Reward Guided Decoding? {#cross-legal-mask-and-reward-tilt}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The mask defines eligible results. Reward expresses preferences within that set. Exponential tilting still multiplies the prior, so neither prior-zero nor mask-zero results can reappear. Replacing a mask with a finite penalty creates a different objective that allows violations to be offset.

    **Illustrative example:** An out-of-stock item may have high predicted revenue but is still excluded by the catalog. Subtracting a little value does not guarantee exclusion.

    Sources: [Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators](../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en.md) · [Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en.md)

### Both TIGER and PLUM predict SIDs. Why doesn't the same next-token loss make them the same training recipe? {#cross-same-sid-not-same-training}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TIGER builds a pipeline from content quantization and sequence generation. PLUM inherits an LLM, aligns language and collaborative spaces using behavior, text, and ASR continual pretraining, and adds co-occurrence and progressive-depth reconstruction in SID-v2. Shared outputs do not equal shared initialization, data, or representation learning. Fix catalog and budget when comparing.

    **Illustrative example:** Two models predict three-level codes. One learns only behavior sequences; the other first sees mixed metadata and behavior. Calling both final losses cross-entropy does not erase that difference.

    Sources: [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [PLUM: Adapting Pre-trained Language Models for Industrial-scale Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2510.07784-plum/README-en.md)

### Why can't Pailitao's complete online gain be attributed causally to Sample–Beam alone? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The online test measures a complete deployment with training data, model, presentation, and blending. A controlled offline ablation supplies different evidence about one module. Local work is documentation only, with no executable interface.

    **Illustrative example:** If transactions rise after changing training data, the model, and blending, the increase cannot all be assigned to the beam recipe simply because it also changed.

    Sources: [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36958-pailitao-mmsearch2/README-en.md)

### Can PinGER prefix diversity replace STATIC's legal mask or guarantee higher TIGER-style offline recall? {#cross-pinger-prefix-spread-versus-static-legality}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. LCP penalties spread slots across parent prefixes as a soft preference. STATIC determines which paths reach valid items. Wider subtree spread can lower recall for one held-out item, as PinGER's table shows. Removing SIDs from inputs, adding diversity, and ensuring legality are different interventions.

    **Illustrative example:** Three semantic categories may each receive beam slots while still containing nonexistent catalog leaves. Removing illegal leaves also does not guarantee retention of the target.

    Sources: [PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en.md) · [Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval](../../../../reproductions/2305.05065-tiger/README-en.md) · [Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators](../../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en.md)

### Can ReuseGR, PinGER and SPADE be reduced to one prefix/diversity score? {#cross-reuse-prior-rank-and-semantic-distance}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not without preserving their distinctions. ReuseGR controls reuse depth and reachable subtrees; PinGER penalizes repeated common-SID-prefix subtrees; SPADE rewards parent rank while producing free-text queries. They act on different objects and stages. Align serving budgets before separately evaluating reachability, redundancy and final quality.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Caching two prefix levels saves computation but need not diversify candidates. Rewarding a lower-ranked free-text query does not calculate its semantic distance from already selected queries.

    Sources: [ReuseGR: Offline–Online Decoupled Generative Retrieval via Adaptive Prefix Reuse](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04259-reusegr/README-en.md) · [SPADE: Spatiotemporal Preference Alignment and Diversity Enhancement for Local Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04662-spade-local-search/README-en.md) · [PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33435-pinger/README-en.md)
